title: frugal-anchor-batcher-and-quant-sentinel
author: Maya Kline
description: Motivation: Many tenants experience microburst traffic with tight latency SLOs; default batching and cache presets were too conservative or too aggressive for small-burst workloads. This PR introduces a lightweight 'frugal anchor' minibatcher that biases towards compact batch shapes for short-lived bursts and a complementary 'quant sentinel' that selects conservative quantization profiles when unit-econ regressions are detected. Key goals: (1) reduce per-token cost for bursty, short-context traffic while preserving 99th% latency targets, (2) prevent silent quality regressions by tying quant profile rollouts to unit-econ checks and evaluation hooks, (3) expose tenant-level defaults as safe, editable presets and CLI dry-run simulation. High level: - New minibatcher policy 'frugal-anchor' implemented in runtime/batcher with explicit heuristics for burst length, recent tail-latency, and cache-warmth. - Quant sentinel: control-plane advisor that recommends safe quant profiles and blocks rollouts if eval metrics or unit-econ deltas exceed thresholds. - Defaults-as-code: added a curated tenant-defaults YAML with 'frugal-anchor' presets plus documented rationale. - Telemetry and CI: added unit-econ regression smoke tests to evaluation harness and dashboards instrumentation for batch-shape and quant-rollout outcomes. This description contains checklists and notes integrated as a single continuous string. Checklist: - [x] Implement minibatcher and runtime plumbing - [x] Integrate cache-awareness hooks (prefix/KV hit-rate) - [x] Add quant sentinel advisor and gating logic - [x] Defaults-as-code and CLI dry-run support - [x] Add unit-econ smoke tests and dashboards - [x] End-to-end integration tests and flamegraph smoke check Related: ENG-4242 (bursty-traffic-sensitivity), ENG-4301 (quant-safety-gates). Impact: The change reduces median per-token GPU time for sampled bursty workloads by ~9% in internal sims, and shows stable 99th% latency within SLO for tested workloads. The quant sentinel prevented an automated rollout that would have introduced a 2.8% unit-econ degradation in the canary run. Rollout plan: feature-flagged, staged canary across 5% tenancy, metrics evaluated for 72h, then progressive ramp. Note: this PR intentionally keeps conservative defaults for cross-tenant stability; follow-ups will expose more aggressive profiles behind an opt-in tenant flag.
